jobs.title: Chief Advancement Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Advancement Officer

Aspen Leadership Group is proud to partner with Cranbrook Educational Community in the search for a Chief Advancement Officer.

Reporting to the President, the Chief Advancement Officer will serve as a key member of Cranbrook Educational Community’s senior leadership team and report directly to the President. This role carries enterprise-wide responsibility for advancing philanthropic strategy and performance across Cranbrook Schools, Horizons-Upward Bound, Cranbrook Academy of Art, Cranbrook Art Museum, Cranbrook Institute of Science, and Cranbrook Center for Collections and Research.

The CAO will play a key leadership role in a comprehensive campaign that, while currently in the quiet phase, is off to a strong start thanks to generous lead gifts; the current team has raised over $130 million towards a working goal of $300 million to support endowment, capital investments, and unrestricted annual needs. In April 2026, the Community announced a landmark $15 million gift to Cranbrook to restore and permanently endow its performing arts center, which in recognition of this historic generosity, will be renamed The Bailey Center for the Performing Arts. This gift is among the most significant philanthropic commitments in Cranbrook's century-long history and is acting as a catalyst for other transformational philanthropy Community-wide.

At the core of the role, the CAO will provide visionary, data-informed leadership to grow and diversify philanthropic revenue, deepen engagement with donors and constituents, strengthen volunteer and board partnerships, and build and lead a high-performing advancement organization.

Cranbrook Educational Community challenges minds and transforms lives. In fulfilling their mission, they provide access to extraordinary education and encourage creativity, innovation, and open inquiry. Cranbrook values and welcomes learners of all ages, backgrounds, and life experiences, preparing them to thrive in and shape a complex world and creatively influence contemporary culture. Cranbrook develops people who will live with purpose and integrity, create with passion, explore with curiosity, and strive for excellence.

Founded by Detroit philanthropists George Gough Booth and Ellen Scripps Booth in 1904, Cranbrook’s 319-acre campus features the work of world-renowned architects such as Eliel Saarinen, Albert Kahn, Steven Holl, Tod Williams and Billie Tsien, Rafael Moneo, Peter Rose, and sculptors Carl Milles, Marshall Fredericks, and others. Critics have called Cranbrook “the most enchanted and enchanting setting in America” and in 1989, it was designated a National Historic Landmark.

Today, Cranbrook Educational Community is comprised of Cranbrook Academy of Art, Cranbrook Art Museum, Cranbrook Center for Collections and Research, Cranbrook House & Gardens, Cranbrook Institute of Science, Cranbrook Schools, and Horizons-Upward Bound.

A bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least ten years of progressive advancement/fundraising leadership experience is required for this position. Cranbrook Educational Community will consider candidates with a broad range of backgrounds. If you are excited about this role and feel that you can contribute to Cranbrook, but your experience does not exactly align with every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply. All applications must be accompanied by a cover letter and résumé. Cover letters should be responsive to the mission of Cranbrook Educational Community and the responsibilities and qualifications specified in the position prospectus.

The target base salary for this position is $275,000 with additional incentive compensation. Cranbrook Educational Community offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, 403(b) and 401(k) retirement plan options, tuition reimbursement, and generous paid time off.

If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, or participating in the selection process, please contact Marianna DiVietro at mariannadivietro@aspenleadershipgroup.com.

To apply for this position, visit: https://opportunities.aspenleadershipgroup.com/opportunities/7253.

jobs.title: Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
JOB POSTING DETAILS

Job Title

Director of Advancement

Job Type

Full Time

Position Level

Experienced

Job Description

Position Overview

The Director of Advancement is a visionary relationship builder and strategic fundraising leader responsible for advancing the mission and long-term sustainability of St. Andrew's Schools through philanthropy, community engagement, and institutional partnerships.

Working closely with the Head of School, Board of Trustees, and Administrative Leadership Team, the Director develops and executes a comprehensive advancement strategy that inspires generosity, deepens constituent engagement, and secures philanthropic support for the school's strategic priorities. This leader cultivates meaningful relationships with alumni, parents, grandparents, foundations, corporations, community leaders, and friends of the school while fostering a vibrant culture of philanthropy grounded in Queen Emma's legacy of compassion, service, and educational opportunity.

Above all, the Director of Advancement understands that philanthropy is about people, purpose, and relationships. Successful fundraising begins with listening, building trust, and helping donors connect their passions with opportunities to make a meaningful difference in the lives of students.

As St. Andrew's Schools begins an exciting new chapter as a fully coeducational PK–12 independent Episcopal school, the Director of Advancement will play a pivotal role in shaping the school's future by securing the philanthropic resources needed to support transformational initiatives, exceptional educational programs, student scholarships, faculty excellence, and campus improvements. This leader will help ensure that the generosity of today's donors creates life-changing opportunities for tomorrow's students, strengthening the school for generations to come.

The Director of Advancement serves as a member of the Administrative Leadership Team and works collaboratively across the school to strengthen community engagement, celebrate the school's impact, and ensure the long-term vitality of St. Andrew's Schools.

What Success Looks Like

During the first 12–18 months, the Director of Advancement will work collaboratively with the Head of School, Administrative Leadership Team, and Board of Trustees to make meaningful progress in the following areas:

Strengthen Philanthropic Relationships

Build authentic relationships with current and prospective donors, expanding the school's pipeline of individual, corporate, and foundation supporters while increasing donor engagement, stewardship, and long-term investment in the mission of St. Andrew's Schools.

Grow a Culture of Philanthropy

Foster a school-wide culture in which trustees, faculty, staff, alumni, parents, grandparents, and friends understand the transformational impact of philanthropy and actively champion the school's mission and strategic priorities.

Increase Sustainable Fundraising

Develop and implement comprehensive fundraising strategies that strengthen annual giving, major gifts, grants, endowment support, and planned giving while diversifying philanthropic revenue and increasing long-term financial sustainability.

Elevate Alumni & Community Engagement

Deepen alumni engagement while strengthening partnerships with community leaders, businesses, foundations, and strategic partners that advance the school's mission and expand its impact throughout Hawai?i.

Strengthen Advancement Infrastructure

Enhance the school's advancement operations through effective donor stewardship, prospect management, data integrity, reporting, and fundraising systems that support long-term organizational excellence.

Advance the School's Strategic Vision

Secure philanthropic support for transformational initiatives, innovative educational programs, faculty excellence, student scholarships, and campus improvements that position St. Andrew's Schools for continued success for generations to come.

Key Areas of Leadership & Responsibility

Strategic Leadership

Develop and implement a comprehensive advancement strategy aligned with the school's mission, strategic priorities, and fundraising goals.

Partner closely with the Head of School to identify philanthropic opportunities and cultivate relationships with major donors, foundations, corporations, and community partners.

Collaborate with the Board of Trustees and Advancement Committee to establish fundraising priorities and long-term philanthropic strategies.

Develop annual advancement plans, measurable goals, and key performance indicators; regularly evaluate progress and recommend strategic adjustments.

Stay current on emerging trends and best practices in philanthropy, donor engagement, and independent school advancement.

Fundraising & Philanthropy

Lead all aspects of annual giving, major gifts, capital campaigns, endowment giving, planned giving, grants, and special fundraising initiatives.

Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward major gift prospects in partnership with the Head of School and Board leadership.

Expand and diversify the school's donor base while strengthening relationships with current supporters.

Research grant opportunities, prepare compelling proposals, and oversee grant compliance and reporting.

Develop strategies that increase donor participation, giving levels, and long-term philanthropic engagement.

Prepare annual fundraising reports that measure institutional progress and celebrate donor impact.

Donor Relations & Stewardship

Design and implement a thoughtful donor stewardship program that reflects the school's values of aloha, kuleana, service, gratitude, and generosity.

Ensure donors receive meaningful recognition, timely communication, and ongoing engagement that inspires continued investment.

Oversee donor prospect research, gift tracking, acknowledgements, recognition, stewardship reporting, and planned giving initiatives.

Collaborate with the Chief Financial Officer to ensure accurate gift recording, endowment reporting, and donor accountability.

Promote a culture of philanthropy throughout the school with the goal of achieving broad participation among trustees, faculty, staff, alumni, parents, grandparents, and friends.

Board & Volunteer Leadership

Serve as staff liaison to the Board of Trustees Advancement Committee.

Collaborate with the Head of School to prepare committee agendas, reports, meeting materials, and strategic recommendations.

Support trustees and volunteer leaders in donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.

Develop fundraising policies and donor engagement strategies for Board consideration.

Community Engagement & Special Events

Lead the planning and execution of major fundraising and community events, including the annual Queen Emma Ball and other donor cultivation activities.

Strengthen alumni engagement through reunions, networking opportunities, volunteer leadership, and lifelong connections to the school.

Represent St. Andrew's Schools throughout the community, cultivating relationships with civic leaders, businesses, foundations, and nonprofit organizations.

Secure sponsorships, auction donations, and strategic partnerships that enhance fundraising success.

Advancement Operations

Provide leadership and supervision for the Advancement Office, including staff development, budgeting, and operational planning.

Ensure the integrity and effective utilization of the advancement database, donor records, prospect management systems, and reporting tools.

Develop and monitor the Advancement Office operating budget.

Manage contracts, software platforms, consultants, and vendor relationships.

Oversee the preservation of the school's historical archives and institutional records.

Strategic Communications

Collaborate with the Marketing and Communications team to develop compelling stories that demonstrate the impact of philanthropy.

Support integrated communication strategies that strengthen donor engagement, alumni relations, and community awareness.

Partner with school leadership to celebrate student success, faculty excellence, and transformational initiatives through print, digital, and social media communications.

Other Responsibilities

Uphold the highest ethical standards consistent with the Association of Fundraising Professionals Code of Ethical Standards and the Donor Bill of Rights.

Support Parent Teacher Fellowship initiatives, including oversight of the school uniform store.

Perform other duties as assigned by the Head of School.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor's degree required.

Master's degree or advanced study in nonprofit management, philanthropy, business, communications, education, or a related field preferred.

Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) credential preferred.

Experience

Minimum of 8–10 years of progressively responsible fundraising and advancement leadership experience.

Demonstrated success securing major gifts and leading comprehensive fundraising programs, including annual, capital, endowment, and planned giving campaigns.
Experience working closely with boards, executive leaders, volunteers, and high-capacity donors.
Experience within an independent school, higher education, healthcare, or nonprofit organization is preferred. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Exceptional relationship-building, networking, and interpersonal skills.
Outstanding written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
Strategic thinker with strong analytical, organizational, and project management abilities.
Demonstrated ability to inspire generosity and cultivate meaningful donor relationships.
High degree of integrity, professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment.
Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
Experience with donor relationship management (CRM) systems such as Raiser's Edge, DonorPerfect, Bloomerang, or similar platforms.
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office Suite, and fundraising technologies.
Ability to work collaboratively across departments while leading with initiative, optimism, accountability, and a solutions-oriented mindset.
Flexibility to attend evening and weekend meetings, donor events, and school functions as needed.

Compensation: $85,000 - $110,000

Personal Qualities

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, mission-driven leader who is energized by building authentic relationships and connecting generous individuals with opportunities to make a lasting difference. They are a compelling storyteller, an excellent listener, and an experienced fundraiser who leads with humility, integrity, gratitude, and optimism. They embrace innovation while honoring tradition and are passionate about helping St. Andrew's Schools thrive for generations to come.

Why St. Andrew's Schools?

Founded in 1867 by Queen Emma Kaleleonālani, St. Andrew's Schools is one of Hawai?i's oldest and most innovative independent schools. Rooted in our Hawaiian and Episcopal heritage, we are committed to developing students who lead with integrity, compassion, courage, and purpose.

As we begin our first year as a fully coeducational PK–12 school, we are entering a transformative period of growth and possibility. This is an extraordinary opportunity for an accomplished advancement leader to partner with an engaged Board of Trustees, dedicated faculty and staff, passionate alumni, generous donors, and an inspiring Head of School to shape the future of one of Hawai?i's most mission-driven educational institutions.

If you are energized by meaningful relationships, inspired by educational excellence, and motivated by the opportunity to make a lasting impact on future generations, we invite you to join us as we continue Queen Emma's legacy of expanding educational opportunity and empowering every learner to Kūlia i ka Nu?u—Strive for the Highest.

Education

Applicant Requirements:

4 Year Degree

Non-discriminatory Statement

jobs.title: Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
Summary/Purpose:
The Director of Advancement provides strategic leadership and oversight for all major and planned gift donor efforts. This position is responsible for designing and executing a comprehensive development program that secures significant philanthropic support ($10,000+) for the Catholic Community Foundation, parishes, schools, and Diocesan ministries. As a key member of the leadership team, the Director supervises the Philanthropy Advisors (Major Gift Officers) staff, manages a donor portfolio, and ensures the Foundation meets annual revenue targets that support the Catholic Community Foundation, parishes, schools, and Diocesan ministries.

Employer:      
Catholic Community Foundation of the Diocese of Richmond (CCF)
Supervisor:    
Executive Director
Salary Range:
$120,000 - $145,000

Responsibilities:

1.     Works with CCF leadership, CCF Board, and CCF staff members to achieve goals and objectives outlined in the CCF’s Strategic Plan. Works with the CCF leadership, CCF board members, and CCF staff to align donor interests with organizational priorities.
2.     Manages the day-to-day work of the Philanthropy Advisors (Major Gift Officers).
3.     Sets individual fundraising targets for staff; conducts annual performance appraisals and provides ongoing coaching in moves management.
4.     Leads the development of individualized major and planned gift solicitation strategies for all portfolios within the Foundation to ensure a pipeline of five-, six-, and seven-figure gifts. Implements and oversees short- and long-term major gift and planned gift strategies to achieve organizational goals and build a culture of philanthropy across the Diocese.
5.     Cultivates and solicits major and planned gifts from a select portfolio of the Foundation’s higher-capacity donors.
6.     Works with the Director of Development and Operations on the budget for major and planned gifts ensuring efficient use of resources for events, travel, and donor cultivation.
7.     Provides regular high-level reporting on performance and pipeline health.
8.     Tracks donor activity, proposals, and outcomes. Prepares reports on fundraising performance and pipeline as requested. Maintains accurate donor records in the Raiser’s Edge NXT database.
9.     Initiates and responds to correspondence with key constituents. Communicates effectively through email and in-person visits.
10.  Creates meaningful engagement opportunities (events, reports, impact stories) and maintains ongoing communication with donors to deepen their commitment to the Catholic Church. 
11.  Assists with review and verification of major gift and planned gift donor recognition lists.
12.  Attends regional and national conferences to advance understanding of fundraising best practices.
13.  Supports capital campaigns, the Annual Diocesan Appeal, and other fundraising activities as requested.
14.  Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree required; 10+ years of demonstrated success in major and planned gifts, with at least 5 years in a supervisory or leadership capacity.
Proven success in personally closing five-, six-, and seven-figure gifts and leading teams to do the same.
Exceptional ability to mentor staff, manage multiple competing priorities, and lead during periods of organizational growth.
Mastery of interpersonal, written, and public speaking skills. Fluency in English and Spanish is preferred.

5.     Advanced understanding of moves management strategies as well as how to analyze wealth screening data and implement it in donor strategy.
6.     Well versed in endowments, charitable gift annuities, trusts, and bequests.
7.     Able to work independently and collaboratively and to multi-task in a fast-paced environment. Accurate, detail-oriented, dependable, and punctual.
8.     Must be proficient in the Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). Experience with Blackbaud’s Raiser’s Edge is preferred. Strong computer skills are required.
9.     Must be able to travel frequently, serve in a full-time capacity, and be available as needed during nights and weekends. 
10.  A background in and appreciation of the Catholic Church and its teachings as well as nonprofit settings is preferred.

Working Conditions: The position of Director of Advancement is a full-time position. The standard office hours are Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. however, office hours may vary weekly depending on special events and visits with donors and other key constituents which may include evenings and weekends. 

Physical Requirements: Light physical effort required. Regularly required to sit for extended periods, stand, walk, reach, bend, lift, listen, talk and perform computer keyboarding. May need to transport campaign materials. Prolonged periods of car traveling.

FLSA Classification: Position is exempt from the overtime and timekeeping provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
REM Community Services,
a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.

Program Director, IDD Services

$59,000 Annually

Have you been looking for a fantastic role to continue your career path in Social and Human Services? Look no further. This role is critical to our success and exemplifies the wonderful mission driven work we do here every day.

Manage the day-to-day operations of one to four programs in a community including organization and implementation of direct supports, person-centered planning, and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, recruiting, retention, staffing, training, safety, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.
Manage program staff members including performance evaluations, scheduling, and orientation.
Make recommendations and/or decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, corrective action, and terminations.
Manage the implementation of program planning; monitor delivery of services and supports; ensure services are consistent, engaging, and relevant to the individuals served.
Must be available on-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.
An equivalent combination of education and experience.
Other education, experience, training, licensure, or certification per state requirements or as required by applicable regulations.
Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to multi-task to meet deadlines.
Effective communication skills to manage relationships.
A reliable, responsible attitude and a compassionate approach.

Why Join Us?

Full compensation/benefits package for full-time employees.
401(k) with company match.
Paid time off and holiday pay.
Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.
Enjoy job security with nationwide career development and advancement opportunities.

We have a rewarding work environment with awesome co-workers – come join our team – Apply Today!

Sevita is a leading provider of home and community-based specialized health care. We believe that everyone deserves to live a full, more independent life. We provide people with quality services and individualized supports that lead to growth and independence, regardless of the physical, intellectual, or behavioral challenges they face.

We’ve made this our mission for more than 50 years. And today, our 40,000 team members continue to innovate and enhance care for the 50,000 individuals we serve all over the U.S.

As an equal opportunity employer, we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Represent St. Andrew's Schools throughout the community, cultivating relationships with civic leaders, businesses, foundations, and nonprofit organizations.

Secure sponsorships, auction donations, and strategic partnerships that enhance fundraising success.

Advancement Operations

Provide leadership and supervision for the Advancement Office, including staff development, budgeting, and operational planning.

Ensure the integrity and effective utilization of the advancement database, donor records, prospect management systems, and reporting tools.

Develop and monitor the Advancement Office operating budget.

Manage contracts, software platforms, consultants, and vendor relationships.

Oversee the preservation of the school's historical archives and institutional records.

Strategic Communications

Collaborate with the Marketing and Communications team to develop compelling stories that demonstrate the impact of philanthropy.

Support integrated communication strategies that strengthen donor engagement, alumni relations, and community awareness.

Partner with school leadership to celebrate student success, faculty excellence, and transformational initiatives through print, digital, and social media communications.

Other Responsibilities

Uphold the highest ethical standards consistent with the Association of Fundraising Professionals Code of Ethical Standards and the Donor Bill of Rights.

Support Parent Teacher Fellowship initiatives, including oversight of the school uniform store.

Perform other duties as assigned by the Head of School.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor's degree required.

Master's degree or advanced study in nonprofit management, philanthropy, business, communications, education, or a related field preferred.

Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) credential preferred.

Experience

Minimum of 8–10 years of progressively responsible fundraising and advancement leadership experience.

Demonstrated success securing major gifts and leading comprehensive fundraising programs, including annual, capital, endowment, and planned giving campaigns.
Experience working closely with boards, executive leaders, volunteers, and high-capacity donors.
Experience within an independent school, higher education, healthcare, or nonprofit organization is preferred. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Exceptional relationship-building, networking, and interpersonal skills.
Outstanding written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
Strategic thinker with strong analytical, organizational, and project management abilities.
Demonstrated ability to inspire generosity and cultivate meaningful donor relationships.
High degree of integrity, professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment.
Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
Experience with donor relationship management (CRM) systems such as Raiser's Edge, DonorPerfect, Bloomerang, or similar platforms.
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office Suite, and fundraising technologies.
Ability to work collaboratively across departments while leading with initiative, optimism, accountability, and a solutions-oriented mindset.
Flexibility to attend evening and weekend meetings, donor events, and school functions as needed.

Compensation: $85,000 - $110,000

Personal Qualities

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, mission-driven leader who is energized by building authentic relationships and connecting generous individuals with opportunities to make a lasting difference. They are a compelling storyteller, an excellent listener, and an experienced fundraiser who leads with humility, integrity, gratitude, and optimism. They embrace innovation while honoring tradition and are passionate about helping St. Andrew's Schools thrive for generations to come.

Why St. Andrew's Schools?

Founded in 1867 by Queen Emma Kaleleonālani, St. Andrew's Schools is one of Hawai?i's oldest and most innovative independent schools. Rooted in our Hawaiian and Episcopal heritage, we are committed to developing students who lead with integrity, compassion, courage, and purpose.

As we begin our first year as a fully coeducational PK–12 school, we are entering a transformative period of growth and possibility. This is an extraordinary opportunity for an accomplished advancement leader to partner with an engaged Board of Trustees, dedicated faculty and staff, passionate alumni, generous donors, and an inspiring Head of School to shape the future of one of Hawai?i's most mission-driven educational institutions.

If you are energized by meaningful relationships, inspired by educational excellence, and motivated by the opportunity to make a lasting impact on future generations, we invite you to join us as we continue Queen Emma's legacy of expanding educational opportunity and empowering every learner to Kūlia i ka Nu?u—Strive for the Highest.

new_jobs.title: Director of Advancement
new_jobs.description:
Summary/Purpose:
The Director of Advancement provides strategic leadership and oversight for all major and planned gift donor efforts. This position is responsible for designing and executing a comprehensive development program that secures significant philanthropic support ($10,000+) for the Catholic Community Foundation, parishes, schools, and Diocesan ministries. As a key member of the leadership team, the Director supervises the Philanthropy Advisors (Major Gift Officers) staff, manages a donor portfolio, and ensures the Foundation meets annual revenue targets that support the Catholic Community Foundation, parishes, schools, and Diocesan ministries.

Employer:      
Catholic Community Foundation of the Diocese of Richmond (CCF)
Supervisor:    
Executive Director
Salary Range:
$120,000 - $145,000

Responsibilities:

1.     Works with CCF leadership, CCF Board, and CCF staff members to achieve goals and objectives outlined in the CCF’s Strategic Plan. Works with the CCF leadership, CCF board members, and CCF staff to align donor interests with organizational priorities.
2.     Manages the day-to-day work of the Philanthropy Advisors (Major Gift Officers).
3.     Sets individual fundraising targets for staff; conducts annual performance appraisals and provides ongoing coaching in moves management.
4.     Leads the development of individualized major and planned gift solicitation strategies for all portfolios within the Foundation to ensure a pipeline of five-, six-, and seven-figure gifts. Implements and oversees short- and long-term major gift and planned gift strategies to achieve organizational goals and build a culture of philanthropy across the Diocese.
5.     Cultivates and solicits major and planned gifts from a select portfolio of the Foundation’s higher-capacity donors.
6.     Works with the Director of Development and Operations on the budget for major and planned gifts ensuring efficient use of resources for events, travel, and donor cultivation.
7.     Provides regular high-level reporting on performance and pipeline health.
8.     Tracks donor activity, proposals, and outcomes. Prepares reports on fundraising performance and pipeline as requested. Maintains accurate donor records in the Raiser’s Edge NXT database.
9.     Initiates and responds to correspondence with key constituents. Communicates effectively through email and in-person visits.
10.  Creates meaningful engagement opportunities (events, reports, impact stories) and maintains ongoing communication with donors to deepen their commitment to the Catholic Church. 
11.  Assists with review and verification of major gift and planned gift donor recognition lists.
12.  Attends regional and national conferences to advance understanding of fundraising best practices.
13.  Supports capital campaigns, the Annual Diocesan Appeal, and other fundraising activities as requested.
14.  Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree required; 10+ years of demonstrated success in major and planned gifts, with at least 5 years in a supervisory or leadership capacity.
Proven success in personally closing five-, six-, and seven-figure gifts and leading teams to do the same.
Exceptional ability to mentor staff, manage multiple competing priorities, and lead during periods of organizational growth.
Mastery of interpersonal, written, and public speaking skills. Fluency in English and Spanish is preferred.

5.     Advanced understanding of moves management strategies as well as how to analyze wealth screening data and implement it in donor strategy.
6.     Well versed in endowments, charitable gift annuities, trusts, and bequests.
7.     Able to work independently and collaboratively and to multi-task in a fast-paced environment. Accurate, detail-oriented, dependable, and punctual.
8.     Must be proficient in the Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). Experience with Blackbaud’s Raiser’s Edge is preferred. Strong computer skills are required.
9.     Must be able to travel frequently, serve in a full-time capacity, and be available as needed during nights and weekends. 
10.  A background in and appreciation of the Catholic Church and its teachings as well as nonprofit settings is preferred.

Working Conditions: The position of Director of Advancement is a full-time position. The standard office hours are Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. however, office hours may vary weekly depending on special events and visits with donors and other key constituents which may include evenings and weekends. 

Physical Requirements: Light physical effort required. Regularly required to sit for extended periods, stand, walk, reach, bend, lift, listen, talk and perform computer keyboarding. May need to transport campaign materials. Prolonged periods of car traveling.

FLSA Classification: Position is exempt from the overtime and timekeeping provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

new_jobs.title: Program Director
new_jobs.description:
REM Community Services,
a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.

Program Director, IDD Services

$59,000 Annually

Have you been looking for a fantastic role to continue your career path in Social and Human Services? Look no further. This role is critical to our success and exemplifies the wonderful mission driven work we do here every day.

Manage the day-to-day operations of one to four programs in a community including organization and implementation of direct supports, person-centered planning, and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, recruiting, retention, staffing, training, safety, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.
Manage program staff members including performance evaluations, scheduling, and orientation.
Make recommendations and/or decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, corrective action, and terminations.
Manage the implementation of program planning; monitor delivery of services and supports; ensure services are consistent, engaging, and relevant to the individuals served.
Must be available on-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.
An equivalent combination of education and experience.
Other education, experience, training, licensure, or certification per state requirements or as required by applicable regulations.
Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to multi-task to meet deadlines.
Effective communication skills to manage relationships.
A reliable, responsible attitude and a compassionate approach.

Why Join Us?

Full compensation/benefits package for full-time employees.
401(k) with company match.
Paid time off and holiday pay.
Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.
Enjoy job security with nationwide career development and advancement opportunities.

We have a rewarding work environment with awesome co-workers – come join our team – Apply Today!

Sevita is a leading provider of home and community-based specialized health care. We believe that everyone deserves to live a full, more independent life. We provide people with quality services and individualized supports that lead to growth and independence, regardless of the physical, intellectual, or behavioral challenges they face.

We’ve made this our mission for more than 50 years. And today, our 40,000 team members continue to innovate and enhance care for the 50,000 individuals we serve all over the U.S.

As an equal opportunity employer, we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by law.
